Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a single source: an AppImage downloaded from `https://nightly.eden-emu.dev/` using a versioned URL based on `_upstream_tag`. The `source` array uses a direct HTTPS URL with a fixed filename, and the checksum is explicitly provided via `sha256sums`, meaning the integrity of the downloaded file will be verified after download. There is no command substitution, dynamic fetching, or execution of remote code during the sourcing of the PKGBUILD.

The global scope contains only variable assignments; no commands are executed at parse time. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so the static `pkgver` is used, which poses no risk. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are not executed under `--noprepare --nobuild`, so the AppImage extraction and modifications occur later and are out of scope for this gate. Downloading and extracting the AppImage is part of the expected workflow and does not imply execution.

The source URL is specific to the project's official infrastructure (`nightly.eden-emu.dev`), and the checksum is pinned, not set to 'SKIP'. Therefore, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and verify the AppImage without executing any untrusted code.
</details>
<summary>
Safe sourcing and source fetch with valid checksums</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt AppImage from the project's official nightly release URL (`https://nightly.eden-emu.dev/`) using a versioned tag that includes a timestamp and Git commit hash. The source is well-defined and matches the upstream project's distribution infrastructure. The provided SHA-256 checksum (`05883e86...`) ensures binary integrity, and there is no use of `SKIP` or checksum omission — the hash is explicitly listed and verifiable.

The build process extracts the AppImage, modifies its desktop file for proper integration (adjusting Exec, Icon, Name, etc.), installs the AppImage into `/opt`, creates a symlink in `/usr/bin`, installs appropriate icons, and registers MIME types for Switch emulator-related file extensions (.nro, .nso, .nsp, .xci). These are standard and expected operations for packaging an AppImage in Arch Linux. The post-install, post-upgrade, and post-remove hooks safely refresh the desktop and MIME databases, which is common practice.

No obfuscated code, unexpected network calls, or dangerous operations (e.g., data exfiltration, dynamic code loading, or execution of external scripts) are present. The operations are transparent, reproducible, and confined to the package's scope. While the source is a binary blob (AppImage), it is checksummed and distributed over HTTPS from the official project domain, which is acceptable for a `-bin` package. No supply-chain red flags are present.
</details>
<summary>
Standard binary packaging with verified checksums; no malicious behavior</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only variable assignments and string expansions with no command substitutions, backticks, evals, or other dangerous operations. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so sourcing the PKGBUILD and running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will not execute any code beyond variable resolution. The `source` array downloads a single AppImage file from the project's own official nightly server (`nightly.eden-emu.dev`) with a fixed SHA-256 checksum. During this gate, `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` prevent the `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions from executing, so the AppImage is not executed or extracted. Therefore, fetching the source and parsing the PKGBUILD poses no risk of code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
<summary>
Top-level code safe; source download from official server.</summary>
</security_assessment>

data.reasoning: PKGBUILD demonstrates safe practices (HTTPS source, pinned checksum, standard installation hooks), but critical executable (AppImage) was skipped in audit.
coverage_issues: Both models skipped Eden-Linux-*.AppImage – the primary executable containing all runtime behavior. This is a critical coverage gap.
false_negatives: AppImage may contain: 1) Network calls during execution 2) Filesystem access outside package scope 3) Dynamic code loading – all unverified due to skipped audit.
learnings: File selection: Prioritize executable binaries in -bin packages. Implement AppImage extraction for content audit.
Assessment quality: Models correctly assessed PKGBUILD but failed to flag binary-skip as critical risk.
Failure mode: Binary skipping creates false negatives. Require explicit risk acknowledgment for skipped executables.
